findings.title: A post-open metadata failure loses descriptor ownership before custody insertion
findings.trigger: In a fresh bounded fixture, let os.open succeed, then inject one ordinary OSError(EIO) in the first os.fstat of that just-opened child directory or leaf; invoke boundary.close after refusal.
findings.expected: Every descriptor opened by the boundary has an owner immediately and is closed on refusal, including failures before identity extraction/custody transfer; no error-dependent growth across evaluations.
findings.actual: Both hooks fired exactly once; close left the opened descriptor live and procfs count changed 8 to 9 for each isolated observation. Only explicit probe remediation closed the leaked FD, restoring 8. The helper calls fstat before any try/finally or registration; neither _fds nor _custody knows this descriptor.
findings.scope: Observed at the actual boundary.read owner path, not through public recompute_scores for this injected error. Public recompute_scores uses the same helpers and its finally closes this same boundary; source inspection establishes that it cannot recover an unregistered descriptor. This pre-existing open-helper gap is material to the explicitly assigned NM03 resource/error closure, not a reopened unrelated historical finding.
findings.impact: Refusal is fail-closed for scores but not for resources. Repeated metadata failures can accumulate live descriptors outside the finite custody registry; an unconditional cleanup/finite-FD claim is unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Keep each successfully opened descriptor under cleanup ownership until transfer into custody succeeds, including metadata/error paths; preserve the original pinned entry on reuse.

findings.title: The custody cap refuses only after opening the excess entry
findings.trigger: Fill a fresh boundary with exactly72 distinct four-byte leaves, then read a73rd leaf while counting actual os.open calls and live descriptors.
findings.expected: After a dedup miss at the internal72-entry cap, refuse before any excess child/leaf open; retain every existing entry and release all resources.
findings.actual: Exact72 succeeds and all old entries remain. The73rd os.open succeeds, transient procfs count grows84 to85, and take then closes the excess FD and raises QS_ARTIFACT_CUSTODY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED:f72. Final boundary cleanup returns8. Thus score refusal and normal finiteness hold, but the explicit before-excess-open obligation does not.
findings.impact: Normal operation has a finite transient bound of4 anchor FDs+72 retained entries+1 unregistered open, rather than the requested4+72 admission bound. No successful aggregate, dropped entry, or unbounded normal growth was observed. This is an internal implementation bound, not a public threshold.
findings.recommendation: Check/reserve capacity after the dedup lookup and before opening a new entry, with exception-safe ownership transfer.
